message:
fix(update): a PID is not an identity, and a stub is not a test

Two corrections, one of them a real defect.

The defect: targets were carried as bare PIDs. Windows reuses those, and the
gap between enumerating a process and waiting on it is long enough for the
original to exit and something unrelated to inherit the number -- at which
point the updater asks a stranger to close. Targets now carry image path and
creation time as well, and an opened handle is checked against both before it
is treated as the process that was meant. A mismatch is not an error; it means
the target is already gone, which is what Quiesce was waiting for. The
enumerator also skips the updater itself.

The other: isolating the tests had turned parts of them into stubs, and a
lambda returning false proves nothing about Windows. So the relaunch failure
is now a real CreateProcessW against a path that does not exist; the rollback
failure is a real file held open with no sharing, so MoveFileEx fails the way
it would in the field; and the lock contention is a real second process -- this
executable re-run with a flag -- because a mutex is re-entrant for its owning
thread and the actual contenders are processes. The contender reports over a
pipe rather than the parent sleeping and hoping.

The PID-reuse case has a control: described with the wrong creation time,
Quiesce returns at once and leaves the process alone; described correctly, the
same call waits and times out. Without the second half the first could pass
for the wrong reason.

registryRoot and serviceName are now required config with no defaults. Nothing
reads them yet -- that is the point. A future RegisterInstall cannot be written
against the real uninstall key and GNLinkSecureInput without failing validate()
first.

The test reports whether it ran elevated and states plainly that the design's
"a host-launched updater needs no second prompt" claim is not checked here.

qwinsta: console active, rdp-tcp listening. 98 checks, up from 64. The three
live product PIDs were unchanged before and after. Still no real process
stopped, no real install directory touched, and nothing fetched over a network.
